name: A London garden

place_source.title: Wikidata: London (Q84), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A narrow back garden behind a row of London terraced houses: a lawn, a border, hawthorn, holly and cypress along the fences and an old apple tree, visited by foxes after dark and by pigeons, tits, magpies and parakeets by day.

facts.text: London has a temperate oceanic climate (Köppen Cfb).

facts.text: London is home to some 10,000 red foxes, as well as hedgehogs and grey squirrels.

source.title: Wikipedia: London

facts.text: Over 60 species of bird nest in central London.

source.title: Wikipedia: London
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "London", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Grey squirrels are not native to Britain: they were introduced from North America in the 1870s as fashionable additions to estates.

source.title: Wikipedia: Eastern gray squirrel

facts.text: Britain's feral rose-ringed parakeets are centred on suburban London; in the winter of 2006, three roosts around the city held about 6,000 birds.
